summary: This paper presents two methods, Gaussian Copula and K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), for generating calibrated prediction intervals (PIs) in vital sign forecasting by leveraging multidimensional Reconstruction Uncertainty Estimate (RUE). The methods are evaluated on two large public healthcare datasets with different temporal resolutions, demonstrating improved uncertainty quantification and interpretability compared to existing approaches.
why_it_matters: Reliable uncertainty quantification in vital sign forecasting is critical for clinical decision-making, as it helps distinguish meaningful warnings from model noise, thereby enabling trustworthy deployment of deep learning models in healthcare settings. The proposed methods enhance the interpretability of forecasts with calibrated prediction intervals sensitive to data shifts.
method_setup: Forecast models predict future vital signs using patient data, with RUE estimating multidimensional uncertainty via reconstruction errors from an autoencoder setup. PIs are constructed by modeling the conditional distribution of prediction errors given reconstruction errors, either parametrically with Gaussian Copula or non-parametrically using KNN on validation sets of similar uncertainty profiles.
key_claims: The Gaussian Copula PI method effectively models prediction error distributions conditioned on multidimensional uncertainty, outperforming conformal prediction baselines on low-frequency vital sign data.
The KNN PI method empirically estimates conditional prediction error distributions, achieving superior performance on high-frequency vital sign data with larger calibration sets.
Multidimensional RUE-based PIs provide improved coverage and interpretability compared to aggregated uncertainty and single-dimensional conformal predictors.
The choice between Gaussian Copula and KNN depends on dataset properties such as calibration set size, error distribution Gaussianity, and temporal resolution.
RUE offers better correlation with prediction error and robustness to false negatives than alternative single-model uncertainty estimators, supporting its effectiveness for vital sign forecasting.
limitations: The accuracy and reliability of RUE-derived PIs depend on the size of the calibration set, with smaller validation sets negatively affecting performance, especially for KNN-based PIs.
The Gaussian Copula method assumes approximate Gaussianity in error distributions, limiting its applicability when this assumption is violated.
Both methods currently require post hoc calibration using validation sets rather than direct training to optimize coverage and interval width.
The evaluation focuses on specific vital sign datasets; generalization to other clinical settings or signal types requires further study.
The proposed methods focus on aleatoric and distributional uncertainty but may not fully capture epistemic uncertainty inherent in model parameters.
evaluates: MIMIC vital signs dataset with minute-level sampling for high-frequency signals.
PhysioNet Challenge 2012 dataset with hour-level sampling for low-frequency signals.
